issues.t: Jerky shifts or slipping into neutral (dual-clutch transmission)
issues.sym: Hesitation or jerks when pulling away or at low speed, the transmission dropping into neutral after coasting in Eco mode, or a transmission warning.
issues.why: Mercedes issued several bulletins for the 8-speed dual-clutch transmission in these years: transmission software that was out of date, a bearing cap cover that didn't meet spec, a mount replacement, and a campaign covering transmission replacement on some vehicles.
issues.next: Ask a Mercedes dealer to check for transmission software updates and open campaigns for your VIN. If it slips or flashes a warning, have it inspected before it gets worse.

issues.t: Water in the footwells can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Wet carpets in the front footwells, a blank instrument cluster, or the engine stalling and not restarting.
issues.why: Water can get in through the front wheel well area and soak electrical parts under the front floor.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for the open recalls and have the dealer seal the wheel wells and repair any damage for free. Dry out wet carpets right away to avoid mold and corrosion.

issues.t: Front axle carrier can rust and fail (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end or steering that feels loose, though there may be no warning before it fails.
issues.why: The carrier that supports the front axle and steering can corrode and weaken, which could cause loss of steering control.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the free inspection done; the carrier is replaced if needed.

issues.t: Stability control unit can be damaged and short (recall)
issues.sym: ABS and stability control warning lights; anti-lock brakes and stability control may not work.
issues.why: The ESP control unit on a small number of SUVs may be damaged, which can disable ABS and stability control and cause a short with fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the unit for free.

issues.t: Airbags may not deploy correctly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. An airbag light may come on in some cases.
issues.why: Several early recalls covered airbag problems: a passenger airbag whose cushion could tear, side curtain airbags that might not deploy properly, a window airbag mounted incorrectly at the front pillar, a wrong driver airbag module on some 2021 models, and restraint software that might not trigger the belts and passenger airbag correctly.
issues.next: Run your VIN through the Mercedes or NHTSA recall lookup and get every open airbag recall done. All repairs are free.

issues.t: Second-row seat may not lock in place (recall)
issues.sym: One side of the second-row seat slides or doesn't latch in its track.
issues.why: The seat may not be aligned in its rail, so it might not lock and could move in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer inspects and corrects the seat for free. Don't seat anyone there if it moves.

issues.t: Spoilers or wheel arch trim can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Rattling or wind noise from the rear hatch area or wheel arches, or trim lifting.
issues.why: Rear and side spoilers and front fender wheel arch covers may not have been welded or installed correctly and can detach on the road.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer inspects and replaces or reattaches the parts for free.

issues.t: Rear power outlet converter can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A hot or burning smell from the second-row power outlet area.
issues.why: The wrong voltage converter for the rear outlet may have been installed, which can put out too much voltage and create a fire risk.
issues.next: Don't use the rear outlet until the dealer has inspected it. The fix is free.

issues.t: Rearview camera image doesn't show (recall)
issues.sym: The screen stays black or reboots when you shift into reverse, so there's no backup camera picture.
issues.why: Software errors in the camera and MBUX multimedia system.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the fix is a free software update, sometimes over the air.

issues.t: Emergency call (eCall) may not work or send wrong location (recall)
issues.sym: An 'SOS not available' message, or no visible sign at all.
issues.why: Software errors in the communication module and its SIM card can stop the automatic crash call or send the wrong location.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the fix is a free software update over the air or at the dealer.

issues.t: Headlights can glare other drivers (recall)
issues.sym: Oncoming drivers flash you, or the beams look aimed too high.
issues.why: The rear axle level sensor linkage for automatic headlight leveling may have been installed wrong.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer inspects and repairs the linkage for free.

issues.t: Door switch corrosion can let the SUV roll away (recall)
issues.sym: The radio or lights stay on after you get out, or the car doesn't seem to know the driver door is open.
issues.why: Moisture can corrode a microswitch in the driver door lock. If it fails, the electronic parking brake or Auto-Park may not engage automatically when the door opens.
issues.next: Always put the SUV in Park and set the parking brake yourself. Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the driver door lock for free, and owners who paid for this repair may be reimbursed.

issues.t: Tires may have sidewall damage (recall)
issues.sym: A bulge or cut in the sidewall of a right-side tire, or sudden air loss.
issues.why: Some new SUVs left the factory with damaged right-side tires.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer inspects and replaces tires for free. Look over your tires and don't drive on a bulging one.

issues.t: Rear brake hoses can rub and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A soft brake pedal, brake fluid warning or fluid near a rear wheel.
issues.why: On some AMG GLB 35s, the rear brake hoses may be routed so they rub and wear through.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN and have the hoses inspected and rerouted for free.

issues.t: Coolant line leak and coolant warning
issues.sym: A coolant level warning, a sweet smell or a small puddle under the front.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a bulletin for a coolant warning caused by a leaking coolant line.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested. Don't drive if the temperature gauge climbs.

issues.t: Won't unlock or start with 'Battery - Start Engine' message
issues.sym: The SUV doesn't unlock or start after sitting, with a battery warning.
issues.why: Mercedes found a control unit can keep the vehicle's data network awake and drain the battery. Another bulletin notes that dealer battery testers could misjudge battery condition.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for the network keep-awake bulletin and software updates before replacing the battery.

issues.t: Humming or vibration from the rear when maneuvering
issues.sym: A hum or vibration from the rear axle when parking or pulling away.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a bulletin for rear axle humming during slow maneuvers.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the bulletin. It is a comfort issue.

issues.t: Creaking or grinding from the steering column
issues.sym: Creaks, squeaks or grinding when turning the wheel, or a vibration in turns below 30 mph.
issues.why: Several bulletins cover steering column noises, rubbing between the steering wheel and the switch module, and a squeaking steering input shaft that needs grease.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to apply the steering noise bulletins.

issues.t: Front brakes squeal
issues.sym: A squeal from the front brakes when stopping, hot or cold.
issues.why: Mercedes traced it to friction between the pad lining and the caliper.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about the brake squeal bulletin; new pads and shims often fix it.

issues.t: MBUX screen or radio freezes
issues.sym: The radio shows a spinning loading wheel and won't start, favorites disappear, Bluetooth drops in calls, or the system reports a hard drive fault.
issues.why: Software and hardware faults in the MBUX infotainment unit, covered by several bulletins.
issues.next: Ask for the latest head unit software. A unit with a hard drive fault needs replacement.

issues.t: Panoramic sunroof glass shatters
issues.sym: A loud bang and broken glass in the panoramic roof, often at highway speed.
issues.why: Owners have reported the panoramic roof glass shattering while driving.
issues.next: Close the sunshade, pull over safely and get the glass replaced. Report it to NHTSA and ask Mercedes whether a recall, warranty extension or goodwill repair covers it.

issues.t: Headlights fog up inside
issues.sym: Fog or water droplets inside the headlight lens.
issues.why: A Mercedes bulletin explains that moisture can pass through the headlight's vent membrane.
issues.next: Light fog that clears after driving is often normal. Large droplets or standing water need a dealer check.

issues.t: Check engine light from crankcase vent line switch
issues.sym: Check engine light with crankcase ventilation codes.
issues.why: A Mercedes bulletin covers fault codes from the crankcase vent line contact switch circuit.
issues.next: Have the codes read; ask the dealer about the bulletin.

issues.t: Mild-hybrid starter-generator software update
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms. The dealer may tell you about it at a service visit.
issues.why: Mercedes found the software coding in the 48-volt belt-driven starter-generator control unit didn't match production specs and opened a service campaign.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check your VIN for the campaign. The update is quick and free.

issues.t: Rear camera cover opens and closes while driving
issues.sym: Clicking or whirring from the rear as the camera cover cycles at slow speed, or the camera recalibrating at every start.
issues.why: Owners have reported the backup camera washer cover moving with Parktronic on. Mercedes says calibration at startup is expected behavior.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for software updates. Don't switch off parking sensors to stop the noise.

issues.t: 'Park Assist inoperative' message
issues.sym: A Park Assist warning on the cluster and parking sensors not working.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a bulletin with test steps for this message.
issues.next: Clean the sensors and have the dealer run the bulletin tests.

issues.t: Right steering wheel buttons don't control the screen
issues.sym: The right-side steering wheel controls don't work the infotainment screen.
issues.why: A Mercedes bulletin calls for an MBUX head unit software update and recoding of the steering wheel electronics.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the software update.

issues.t: Tire repair sealant bottle may leak
issues.sym: Sticky sealant in the cargo area, or the tire repair bottle missing.
issues.why: Mercedes found some TIREFIT sealant bottles from one supplier might not meet spec and could leak.
issues.next: Check the bottle in the cargo area. Ask the dealer to check your VIN for the campaign.
